correctness.rationale: The Hadamard graph has intersection array {n,n-1,n/2,1;1,n/2,n-1,n}. From the five adjacency sectors n, sqrt(n),0,-sqrt(n),-n with multiplicities 1,n,2n-2,n,1, the distance-j eigenvalues are (1,n,2n-2,n,1), (1,sqrt(n),0,-sqrt(n),-1), (1,0,-2,0,1), (1,-sqrt(n),0,sqrt(n),-1), and (1,-n,2n-2,-n,1). Weighted d^p eigenvalues yield exactly p<=1 and the two nontrivial inequalities. Centered Gram rank subtracts equality-sector multiplicities, including the n=4 Hamming special case. Exponential eigenvalues factor into (1-z²)(1±sqrt(n)z+z²), (1-z²)², and (1-z)²(1-(n-2)z+z²); n-2>=sqrt(n) makes the last the binding condition, leading to arcosh threshold. Distinct embedded points ensure strict PD of Gaussian powered distance for positive scale. Independently reconstructed Sylvester Hadamard graphs n=4,8,16 and numerically matched spectral sectors.
residual_risks: Numerical n<=16 tests are not proof for all Hadamard orders.
